content.comment_body: I purchased the [product_name] kit, which includes a CD for [product_name] software, but my desktop and Surface Pro do not have CD drives. Is there a way to transfer the CD contents to a USB drive and use that for installation on my Surface Pro? I have access to another PC with a CD drive, but I'm unsure if transferring the software files onto USB is allowed or if the CD itself acts as the license key. Any advice would be appreciated. Thanks!
The CD contains the license. You can copy the contents from the CD onto a USB drive and complete the installation from USB.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is unable to install [product_name] software because the provided CD format is incompatible with current devices that lack optical drives. Licensing requirements and installation portability cause further confusion, highlighting a challenge when old media formats are used with new hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks a simple, license-compliant way to install [product_name] software without a CD drive, expecting a hassle-free solution for devices that only support USB installation.
